fb_burryman.text: Every August a man walks round this town covered in burrs. Head to toe. They stick to him and he sticks to the route, nine hours of it, and folk give him a dram through a straw.
Is it for luck? Is it to chase off bad spirits? Is it because it's August? Aye. All of those.

fb_seal_watcher.text: Grey seals on the rocks there. Grey seal pups are born white and fluffy in the autumn, and they can't swim for weeks. Not my favourite fact. My favourite is that they sing.
Puffins nest out on the Isle of May, further down the firth, and the gannets on the Bass Rock make it look snowy from the shore. The whole Forth is heaving with birds.

fb_culross_guide.text: Culross's laird, Sir George Bruce, dug a coal mine that ran out under the Forth, with a shaft on an artificial island in the sea. King James VI came to visit, came up the shaft, saw water all round him and thought he'd been kidnapped.
The palace is ochre because it's harled and limewashed. People call the colour Culross yellow. It glows on a dull day, and Fife has a lot of dull days to practise on.

fb_seal_1.text: The seal opens one eye, decides you are not a fish, and closes it again.

fb_seal_2.text: A seal pup flumps along the sand towards you, then thinks better of it and flumps back.
